text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Slovenian newspapers:

- Unofficial results of Sunday's referendum after 98.4 percent counted votes showed that none of the three options for a new electoral system won the necessary 50 percent backing to be adopted. Latest figures showed that turnout was only 37.7 percent, much lower than November's general elction turnout at 73.7 percent.
- Slovenia's 17-year-old ski jumper Primoz Peterka won a World Cup ski jumping event in Kuusamo (Finland) on Sunday.
- Losses of Slovenian Railways are expected to reach 3.2 billion tolars ($22.9 million) by the end of this year, the company's general manager Marjan Rekar said.

- Slovenian President Milan Kucan will start two-day official talks with representatives of all political parties on Monday. After talks are finished Kucan is expected to propose his candidate for prime minister.

- Slovenia's ombudsman said that during electoral referendum on Sunday he received 32 complaints from voters, mostly over violations of breaking a convention that no campaigning should take place a day before a poll.
- Minister of Economic Relations and Development Janko Dezelak will participate in conference of the World Trade Organisation in Singapoore starting on Monday.
- Number of employed people in September fell 2.2 percent to 859,416 compared to the same month last year, the Slovenian Statistical Office said.
